summary: Frontend-only redesign regression executed on public URL. Upload -> Processing -> Results -> Analytics core flow works with JD+ZIP submission, polling transition, results controls, export trigger, and analytics chart rendering. One critical navigation regression found.

ui_bugs.issue: After completing a batch and returning to Upload page, nav results/analytics links still point to '/' and do not navigate to latest batch routes.

integration_issues.flow: Cross-page route flow after successful screening
integration_issues.issue: Batch id is saved in localStorage but ShellLayout nav links do not update reactively in-session, breaking expected route continuity.

action_items: Fix ShellLayout nav link target derivation so Results/Analytics links react to newly created batch IDs without requiring a hard refresh.
Recommended approach: store last batch id in React state/context (or derive from router/search params) instead of direct localStorage read during static render.
Re-test full route flow: results -> upload -> nav results/nav analytics after fix.
critical_code_review_comments: ShellLayout reads localStorage directly (`const batchId = localStorage.getItem(...)`) with no reactive state subscription, causing stale nav href values during SPA transitions.
Results/Analytics nav targets are computed from this non-reactive value, so links can remain '/' even when localStorage has a valid batch id.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core redesigned pages render and key controls work. Repro for critical bug: run a batch to results, click top nav Upload, then inspect nav-results-link/nav-analytics-link hrefs (both become '/'); clicking them keeps user on Upload despite localStorage containing batch id.
rca of the issue: Root cause: stale non-reactive batch id source in ShellLayout. `batchId` is read from localStorage at render time and not wired to state/events; after localStorage update from upload flow, top nav links are not recomputed reliably in active SPA session. Mitigation: keep batch id in state/context and update on successful submission (or listen to storage + route state), then derive nav routes from reactive source.
